FPS TARGET: a steady 30 fps on every screen and platform (GBA, PS1, Dreamcast), logic at 30 ticks a second, no frame over 33 ms; combat stays as SP8 left it. The measurements and the package list this wave works from: docs/design/held/SPEED_AUDIT2.md (sections 4-6); the tooling: tools/speed2.py, make -C gba test-speed2 / profile-speed2, ps1/harness/speed2.sh, dc/harness/speed2.sh (docs/GBA.md "Speed tour 2" and the "Speed wave 2: S2-x" sections, docs/PS1.md "Speed tour 2"). Landed: S2-1..S2-8, S2-12, S2-13 and the analog sticks. In flight on this machine (do not duplicate): PS1-RAM (PS1 resident memory; until it lands the PS1 margin is only 65,952 B, so add NO resident PS1 bytes), S2-9 (workshop), S2-10 (saves and loads), S2-11 (house turn), S2-4b (the Fun Fair, which extends S2-4's kept-playfield mechanism in core/src/mg*.c and the GBA backdrop baker: if you use the same baker, keep your change to it small and expect to rebase onto theirs), G2-EX (exorcism), and speed audit 3 (a fresh measurement of every scene: docs/design/SPEED_AUDIT3.md when it lands; use its numbers if it has landed when you start).

OWNER DECISION 2026-11-13 (VISUAL TRADE-OFFS APPROVED): the owner read the list of scenes that cannot reach 30 on the GBA without a visual trade-off (docs/design/SPEED_AUDIT3.md section 6) and said: do those fixes. So where exact steps do not close the gap, take the trade-offs of that table: skies, floors, flame walls, LED walls, beams, fog and auras redrawn at 15 Hz and kept between their steps (the foreground, the cursor, the characters, the bubble and the choice stay at 30), straight bands instead of a wavy sky, fewer and wider flame bars, fewer or slower fog puffs, still back rows of a crowd as hardware sprites where OBJ VRAM allows. Do them on the GBA only; where the PS1 and the Dreamcast already hold 30 they stay as they are (the GBA may look a little simpler than the PS1: say so in the docs). Every such change is listed with before / after screenshots (SPEED DEFAULTS). The goal is a steady 30 fps, logic 30, no frame over 33 ms: try the smallest trade first, add the next one only if the measured number needs it, and write down which trades were taken and which were not needed.

packages.title: Kitchen at a steady 30
packages.brief:
Speed S2-4, the kitchen family (docs/design/held/SPEED_AUDIT2.md sections 4-6, causes C3 and C1; GBA rank 6): the kitchen (the cook book, chop, stir, fry, bake, simmer, the result, the counter) ran at 17-22 fps on the GBA at audit 2, because the static backdrop is redrawn every frame; on the PS1 the kitchen counter had single 50-67 ms frames. S2-1's modal hold has landed since and may already have lifted the popups: measure first (make -C gba test-speed2 with the group that holds the kitchen windows, then profile-speed2 on the windows under 30).
Goal: every kitchen and cooking window of the speed2 scripts at a steady 30 drawn fps, logic 30, no frame over 33 ms on the GBA; no frame over 33 ms on the PS1; the Dreamcast unchanged.
How: the static layer drawn once and kept (a retained panel, or both Mode 4 pages), each tick restoring only the rectangles under what moved and drawing the movers (SP7's record / replay of rect lists, S2-4's kept playfield and baker in docs/GBA.md "Speed wave 2: S2-4"); divisions in the painters through reciprocal tables. Exact where possible (frame hashes); pixel-changing steps listed with screenshots. Files: core/src/cook*.c, fishcook*.c as needed, gba/src. EWRAM / IWRAM: net zero; say what ROM it adds.

packages.title: Dreams at a steady 30
packages.brief:
Speed S2-4, the dreams family (docs/design/held/SPEED_AUDIT2.md sections 4-6, cause C3 plus the dim; GBA rank 4): every dream vignette, the nightmare and the wake-up choice ran at 10.6-13 fps with logic at 17.6-25 ticks a second on the GBA at audit 2 (slow motion, the worst kind of miss); on the PS1 the nightmare vignettes and the choice had single 50-67 ms frames. S2-1's modal hold has landed since: measure first (make -C gba test-speed2 with the group that holds the dream windows, then profile-speed2 on what is under 30).
Goal: every dream window of the speed2 scripts at a steady 30 drawn fps with logic at 30 and no frame over 33 ms on the GBA; no frame over 33 ms on the PS1; the Dreamcast unchanged.
How: the dream rooms and skies are static backdrops: draw them once and keep them (retained panel / kept pages / baked like S2-4's playfield), fold the dim into the kept picture instead of shading every frame, restore only under what moves. Exact where possible (frame hashes); pixel-changing steps listed with screenshots. Files: core/src/dream*.c, gba/src. EWRAM / IWRAM: net zero; say what ROM it adds.
TRADE-OFFS APPROVED BY THE OWNER (2026-11-13) for what exact steps cannot close (docs/design/SPEED_AUDIT3.md section 6, "Dreams"): the sky and the floor redrawn at 15 Hz and kept between their steps (foreground, bubble and wake-up choice stay at 30); if that is still short, a simpler sky (straight bands instead of the wave). Measure after each trade and stop when the window holds 30 drawn fps, logic 30, no frame over 33 ms. Report which trades were needed.

packages.title: Concert at a steady 30 on the GBA
packages.brief:
The Fun-Fair concert / music show on the GBA runs at about 20 drawn fps after SP6 (docs/GBA.md: the SP6 concert section and its ledger row; ROADMAP "SP6"; the profile target make -C gba profile-concert; the PS1 side was fixed by P-K1 and holds 30: docs/PS1.md). The owner's target is a steady 30 fps, logic 30, no frame over 33 ms, in all three concert shows and the choir.
Goal: close that gap on the GBA. Start from SP6's own notes on what was left and a fresh profile of each show on today's tree. Exact steps first (frame hashes); then pixel-changing steps under SPEED DEFAULTS (kept stage parts, crowd and beams at half rate, sprites as OBJ like the PERFORM choir), each with before / after screenshots and a line in the docs. The PS1 (three shows at 30 on PCSX-Redux, ps1/harness/scripts/perf_concert.txt) and the Dreamcast must not get slower. If a show still cannot hold 30, land what helps and write the measured number, the gap and what it would take. Files: core/src/concert*.c, gba/src. EWRAM / IWRAM: net zero.
TRADE-OFFS APPROVED BY THE OWNER (2026-11-13) (docs/design/SPEED_AUDIT3.md section 6, "Concert band and choir"): the LED wall and the beams at 15 Hz kept between their steps, the crowd's back rows as hardware sprites where OBJ VRAM allows, fewer and wider flame bars.
CHOIR EXPERIMENT (owner's own idea, 2026-11-13: "scale the singers in the choir smaller and see if that does something"): the choir shows up to 16 scaled chibis (blits 12.6 ms, flame wall 15, beams and checkers 8.4 of a 46.9 ms frame at audit 3). Make the singers' scale a parameter and measure the choir window at today's size and at roughly 85%, 75%, 66% and 50% of it (drawn fps, work ms per tick, frames over 33 ms), with and without the other trades. Put the table (scale, fps, ms, what it looks like) into docs/GBA.md and into your report, and screenshots of each scale into the evidence directory. Then keep the largest scale that lets the choir hold 30 together with the smallest other trades; if no scale reaches 30, keep the best one that is still readable and say what the gap is. Also say plainly what the scaling did on its own: that is the answer the owner asked for. GBA only (the PS1 choir holds 30 at today's size); the singers keep their looks (hair, colours, faces), only the size changes.
